what_it_does: Large AI training runs — jobs that can use thousands of expensive GPUs for weeks — are regularly interrupted by hardware failures (a GPU overheating, a memory error, a network glitch), but there has been surprisingly little rigorous measurement of how often these failures occur and how much useful work is actually lost as a result. This paper reports findings from watching two large clusters of Nvidia A100 GPUs over eleven months, covering 4 million jobs totaling over 150 million GPU-hours of actual usage. The researchers built a mathematical model of how failure rates change with job size (larger jobs using more GPUs fail more often simply because there are more components that can break), and derived a formula for 'Effective Training Time Ratio' — the fraction of time a training job actually makes forward progress versus time lost to failures and restarts. This formula lets operators predict how much a simple fix like saving checkpoints more often (so that when something breaks, less work is re-done) would improve real-world training efficiency.
